EWM is gaining huge popularity across all the industries.
This chapter delineates the various features and benefits offered by SAP EWM
catering to the business requirements of diverse warehouses across industries.
We’ll cover the advantages when considering SAP EWM as an implementation
solution for your warehouses, including the return on investment it offers.
Additionally, this chapter considers the progression and evolution of SAP EWM
over the years, including the step-by-step process and features added with every
release.
Furthermore, this chapter imparts detailed information about the various
deployment options offered by SAP to implement SAP EWM solutions. This
information can help you identify the appropriate deployment option based on
your business and warehouse needs, resource availability, and investment
considerations, both in the short term and the long term. This chapter also
encompasses diverse master and transactional data techniques for bringing
data from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA into SAP EWM for deployment.
Towards the end of this chapter, you’ll understand the integration of SAP EWM
with various SAP modules and business processes across all industries,
showcasing SAP’s unique selling points. Finally, we conclude with a summary of
how SAP EWM is being accepted by customers across industries.
1.1 What Is Extended Warehouse Management?
SAP EWM is a sophisticated solution for efficiently managing warehouse
operations. You can digitally oversee your warehouse processes such as
receiving, storage, goods transportation, inventory tracking, and shipment,
including shipments of products to both customers and distribution centers.
SAP EWM is tailor-made to meet the demands of extensive and intricate
warehouse and distribution networks dealing with high volume and high
velocity in goods movements. SAP EWM offers automated and adaptable
assistance for handling different types of goods movements and inventory
management within your warehouse complex. The system further streamlines
logistics processes within warehouses to enhance overall efficiency.

20
SAP EWM empowers you to digitally map your entire warehouse complex down
to the storage bin level, thus providing a comprehensive overview of product
quantities within your warehouses. The solution also enables your warehouse
operation teams to locate specific products within a warehouse complex at any
time. Through SAP EWM, warehouses can optimize storage bin usage and stock
movements and even store stock from multiple plants in a randomly managed
warehouse.
The SAP EWM solution has emerged as a pivotal element in the storage and
distribution operations of many organizations. This application enables you to
leverage technologies that enhance transparency, maximize fulfillment
efficiency, and improve customer service, ultimately optimizing the business.
Through SAP EWM, you can streamline warehouse processes, improve inventory
accuracy, and gain real-time visibility into your supply chain operations. By
harnessing the power of SAP EWM, your organization can more effectively
manage its warehouse and distribution processes, can reduce costs, and can
enhance its overall competitiveness in the market.
SAP EWM utilizes powerful automation technologies and optimization techniques
in conjunction with logistics and fulfillment processes. The application
encompasses all aspects of warehouse and distribution management, including
multichannel fulfillment and distribution, inventory management and control,
cross-docking processes, labor management, and billing for companies of all
sizes and across industries.
SAP EWM facilitates the efficient management of inbound and outbound
processes, as well as the management of storage and retrieval operations. The
solution is particularly well suited for businesses with high-volume warehouses
and provides automated support for goods movement and inventory
management. Procurement, shipping, production supply, and receipt processes
can be consistently organized and monitored, with integration capabilities for
quality management, transportation, and foreign-trade compliance. Advanced
functionalities such as value-added services, kitting, labor planning and
management, yard management, and analytics offer complete visibility into
inventory and logistics. Additionally, cross-docking, importing/exporting,
quality management, picking from goods receipts, and push deployments are
included. SAP EWM integrates easily with cutting-edge technologies, including
pick by voice, augmented reality (AR), radio frequency identification (RFID),
material handling equipment, automated guided vehicles (AVGs), and
warehouse robots.

21
SAP EWM offers intelligent inbound processing management capabilities that
optimize key processes, such as the following:
Receipt and validation of advanced shipping notifications (ASNs)
Goods receipt and optimization of receipt processes
Determination of putaway and putaway bins
Internal routing for detailed modeling and tracking of warehouse movements
Deconsolidation to streamline putaway through sorting and packing goods
during receiving
Returns management, including for e-commerce, to efficiently identify and
dispose of returned goods back into the supply chain
Direct receipt from production
Transportation unit (TU) management
SAP EWM streamlines the management of storage and internal processing by
offering the following features:
Simple physical inventory processes and record validation to reduce
inventory counting efforts and manage inventory balances effectively
Slotting, replenishment, rearrangement, and stock consolidation capabilities
to optimize storage and improve facility utilization
Kitting and value-added services for faster time-to-market and personalized
product offerings
Automated warehouse billing to facilitate activity-based electronic billing of
warehouse expenses to customers and payment to warehouse vendors
SAP EWM offers advanced features that can enhance the speed and flexibility of
outbound processes in the warehouse, such as the following:
Direct outbound delivery
This feature streamlines the outbound process and reduces the time and
costs associated with intermediate warehousing and handling by allowing for
direct delivery of goods to customers.
Warehouse order creation , wave management, wave management ,
route planning, route planning , and picking bin determination, and
picking bin determination

These features optimize the routing and picking of goods, ensuring timely
planning and delivery of customer orders.
Picking , packing, packing , staging, loading management, staging,
loading management , and goods issue
Efficient management of these features ensures that goods are picked,
packed, staged, and loaded accurately and in a timely manner.
Optimal work assignment
This feature ensures that work is assigned to the most suitable personnel,
considering their skill set and availability, to increase overall efficiency.
TU management
This feature enables the efficient management of vehicle flows within a
warehouse to facilitate shipping and receiving operations.
Kitting for customer-specific orders
This feature customizes orders to meet the specific needs of customers, thus
enhancing customer satisfaction.
Production supply and staging
These features optimize production planning, reduce the risk of stockouts,
and enable synchronized material flows and accurate inventory visibility
between your warehouses and your production facilities.
SAP EWM offers a range of cross-functional capabilities related to the movement
of materials. These capabilities include planned and opportunistic cross-docking,
stock-specific units of measurement, and labor management. Additionally, the
software provides optimization for work package creation, resource allocation,
and stock consolidation. By utilizing the software’s advanced functionalities, you
can efficiently manage packaging specifications, batches, serial numbers, catch
weights, and dock appointment scheduling.
In addition, the SAP Warehouse Insights solution empowers you to enhance,
visualize, and analyze your warehouse operations, allowing for improved
resource utilization and real-time monitoring of resources through Internet of
Things (IoT) services. SAP EWM is a comprehensive solution that provides a
robust tool for managing warehousing and logistics. With this software, you can
seamlessly orchestrate your processes from beginning to end and streamline
your global logistics and warehousing operations.
Regarding the automation of warehouses, SAP EWM’s material flow system
component offers direct control and monitoring capabilities for automated
© 

23
storage and retrieval systems. It enables the direct control of programmable
logic controllers (PLCs) used in high-rack storage, small-parts warehousing,
shuttle warehousing, and more. The integrated material flow system can help
you manage the movement of units within automated systems, control conveyor
segments, and monitor operations at various levels. Additionally, the application
manages material handling equipment for distribution vehicles, sorters, and
label applicators. This functionality supports pallets, containers, and cartons, as
well as pick, pack, and pass technologies. Warehouse users can access and
execute their tasks flexibly on a wide range of mobile devices, such as handheld
radio frequency (RF) terminals, tablets, smartphones, wireless scanners, and
printers, as well as wearable devices like voice headsets and smart glasses. This
approach can improve employee engagement and user efficiency by allowing
employees to use technologies they are already familiar from their personal
lives, thereby streamlining operations.
SAP EWM facilitates intelligent warehousing within the SAP S/4HANA framework.
By incorporating SAP EWM, you can streamline your IT infrastructure and
enhance operational efficiency. The platform provides cutting-edge capabilities,
such as in-memory analytics and advanced user interfaces (UIs). Depending on
your organizational requirements, you can opt for a decentralized
implementation for expansive, high-volume warehousing with decentralized
Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (decentralized EWM) or an
embedded module for smaller and mid-sized enterprises with embedded
Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM).
Furthermore, SAP EWM is available on the cloud, allowing for greater scalability,
quicker implementation, and reduced cost of ownership.
SAP Best Practices packages provide preconfigured solutions and modules for
SAP EWM, making the implementation process fast and easy. SAP offers flexible
licensing options for deploying embedded EWM application, which can be
customized to suit individual business requirements. The basic warehouse
management module focuses on inventory management, inbound and
outbound processing, goods movement, and reporting to provide transparency
and control over stock. The advanced warehouse management module offers
additional features such as material flow control, yard management, labor
management, value-added services, kitting, cross-docking, and warehouse
billing to optimize warehouse processes. Both levels of SAP EWM can serve as a
pathway towards supply chain convergence in SAP S/4HANA.

SAP EWM is a comprehensive solution for managing your warehousing and
logistics operations globally. It streamlines your processes from planning and
storage to picking, packing, and shipping, leading to enhanced efficiency, speed,
and adaptability. With SAP EWM, you can take advantage of various features,
including the flexibility to customize your warehouse layout and processes, to
gain real-time visibility into inventory and operations, to optimize storage
planning, and to maximize space utilization. The system also includes automatic
wave planning to increase throughput, efficient warehouse order management,
and work package creation for seamless process execution. Furthermore, SAP
EWM enables you to offer value-added services, such as creating kits and
modules, and to directly control automated warehouses.
Designed to help you comply with regulations across multiple countries, the
application offers a comprehensive set of features to meet international trade
processing and sustainability requirements.

1.2 The Progression of Extended Warehouse
Management
In this section, we’ll discuss the evolution of SAP EWM. We’ll start with the pre-
SAP S/4HANA versions, then discuss embedded EWM and decentralized EWM in
SAP S/4HANA, along with cloud-based options for SAP EWM.
1.2.1 SAP EWM with Non-SAP S/4HANA (SAP EWM 5.0 to SAP
EWM 9.5)
As shown in Figure 1.1, in 2006, SAP released their initial version of the SAP EWM
software, SAP EWM 5.0, alongside their service parts management solution. As a
critical component of service parts management, SAP EWM was designed to
seamlessly integrate with SAP’s supply chain execution platform, streamlining
the planning, execution, and monitoring of goods movements across supply
chain networks. Since its introduction, SAP EWM has undergone significant
development and improvements through subsequent releases, making it one of
the top WMSs available today.
Figure 1.1 SAP EWM’s Progression
In 2006, the last significant development in the logistics execution system was
made available in SAP ERP 6.0, while SAP EWM 5.0 was already in the “ramp-up”
process. With the introduction of a new system philosophy, the first release of
SAP EWM 5.0 included new and existing processes and functions using a
completely new system basis and document structure. Organizational units
were taken from the old logistics execution system and enhanced by new ones.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

26
The release of SAP EWM 5.1 in 2008 was another important milestone in the
history of SAP warehouse logistics. With the new material flow system
component, SAP EWM now features a fully integrated material flow calculator,
significantly improving upon the old logistics execution system.
In SAP EWM 7.0, released in 2009, SAP has closed the process gap in production
supply that had existed. The process area was supplemented by opportunistic
cross-docking as well as merchandise distribution cross-docking.
In SAP 7.01, released in 2010, expansions were included for the material flow
system. On the performance side, the response times of telegram exchange were
improved, and the available functions now also covered requirements related to
controlling container conveyor equipment.
Released in 2011, SAP EWM 7.02 reflected the ultimate replacement of the old
logistics execution system. Migration tools were used to move master data and
processes from logistics execution systems, and the rapid-deployment solution
(RDS) facilitated the fast deployment and conversion to SAP EWM.
With the release of SAP EWM 9.0 in 2013, SAP combined its three most crucial
systems for operative logistics—Extended Warehouse Management (EWM),
Transportation Management (TM), and Event Management (EM)—onto the
common system platform for supply chain execution. This move offered
significant potential for optimizing the entire supply chain. Apart from the
integration with TM and EM, SAP EWM 9.0 offered many new functions. In terms
of changing quantities in delivered packaging, standard SAP EWM 9.0 provided a
solution of using stock-specific units of quantity, which significantly facilitated
the goods issue processes with different packaging units.
Subsequent releases included SAP EWM 9.1 in May 2014, 9.2 in April 2015, 9.3 in
November 2015, 9.4 in May 2016, and 9.5 in November 2017. SAP includes
additional functions in labor management, improvements in retail and e-
commerce, and the integration of SAP Global Batch Traceability (SAP GBT).
SAP EWM 9.5 was the last version based on the supply chain management
platform, with the successor release based on an SAP S/4HANA system that can
be used as an embedded EWM solution or a decentralized EWM solution. The
SAP EWM system, as an application in SAP’s supply chain management solution,
is designed as a decentralized WMS that can be deployed together with SAP
Advanced Planning and Optimization or with global available-to-promise (global
ATP) on one system.

27
1.2.2 Embedded EWM and Decentralized EWM
SAP S/4HANA is a cutting-edge enterprise resource planning (ERP) solution that
incorporates SAP EWM capabilities. SAP EWM is a WMS that can handle complex
logistics operations with real-time visibility and control. Since its introduction in
SAP S/4HANA 1610, SAP EWM has been gaining in popularity as a comprehensive
solution for managing warehouses of all sizes. One significant benefit of
embedded EWM is its ability to leverage the advanced processing capabilities of
SAP HANA, a high-performance in-memory database platform that provides real-
time insights into operations. This integration enables you to significantly
reduce the total cost of ownership (TCO) compared to using standalone or
decentralized EWM systems.
SAP has been continually improving and enhancing SAP EWM to cater to the
diverse warehousing needs of its customers. In September 2018, embedded
EWM for SAP S/4HANA 1809 was launched. This update introduced several new
features to enhance the functionality of SAP EWM, such as the ability to reuse
ERP delivery numbers in SAP EWM for both outbound and inbound deliveries.
In September 2019, embedded EWM for SAP S/4HANA 1909 was introduced,
highlighting the enhanced integration between SAP EWM and SAP
Manufacturing Execution. This integration allows for better coordination and
collaboration between the two systems, leading to more efficient warehouse
and production processes. The increased integration also helps companies
optimize their resource utilization, leading to better efficiency and productivity.
In October 2020, embedded EWM was launched with various new features to
enhance warehouse visibility. The update includes improved analytical
capabilities that provide better insights into warehouse operations, enabling
companies to make data-driven decisions and optimize their processes. The new
analytical capabilities allow users to track key performance indicators (KPIs)
such as warehouse utilization, stock accuracy, and delivery performance in real
time. Users can monitor and analyze warehouse performance, thus enabling
quick identification and resolution of issues.
In SAP S/4HANA 1809, Feature Pack Stack (FPS) 01, SAP unveiled a new
deployment option called decentralized EWM. This deployment option maintains
the SAP EWM system as a distinct entity while still utilizing separate SAP ERP or
SAP S/4HANA core systems. This option enables companies to choose the
deployment alternative that best fits their specific needs and requirements.

28
Overall, the inclusion of embedded EWM offers businesses a powerful
warehouse management solution with enhanced capabilities to improve their
operations, increase efficiency, and ultimately drive business growth.
1.2.3 Cloud-Based SAP EWM
SAP EWM has an extensive and noteworthy history of development and
evolution, with both on-premise and cloud-based versions available. The cloud-
based version of SAP EWM was initially launched in 2017, as part of the release of
SAP S/4HANA Cloud, with the primary objective of providing an easy-to-use,
flexible, and scalable warehouse management solution that caters to businesses
of all sizes, especially those that have intricate supply chain networks.
The cloud-based version of SAP EWM exploits the latest cutting-edge
technologies and is highly interoperable with other cloud-based solutions, such
as SAP TM, SAP Global Trade Services (SAP GTS), and SAP Integrated Business
Planning for Supply Chain (SAP IBP), to name a few. This integration enables
businesses to manage their entire supply chain operations from a unified
platform, streamlining their processes and boosting productivity.
Since its inception, SAP EWM Cloud has undergone several updates and
enhancements, aimed at refining the user experience (UX), fortifying analytics
capabilities, and bolstering integration with other SAP cloud solutions. The
latest iteration of SAP EWM Cloud is version 2108, released in August 2021. This
newest version incorporates sophisticated features like intelligent wave
management, superior integration with SAP TM, and enhanced automation
capabilities.
These features enable elevated levels of operational efficiency, allowing
businesses to optimize their warehouse management and overall supply chain
operations.

29
1.3 System Environment and Deployment
Options
The deployment options available for SAP EWM are shown in Figure 1.2. These
options are diverse and flexible, tailored to the specific business requirements
and IT infrastructure of an organization. The deployment of SAP EWM can vary
depending on an organization’s IT landscape and business needs.
Figure 1.2 SAP EWM Deployment Options
SAP provides several deployment options, including the following:
On-premise deployment
This option involves the installation and operation of SAP EWM on the
organization’s own servers, which are managed by their IT department. This
model is ideal for organizations that want complete control over their IT
infrastructure and have the necessary resources to manage it.
Cloud deployment
This option deploys SAP EWM on a cloud infrastructure like Amazon Web
Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP). This option
provides a flexible and scalable deployment model, where an organization
only pays for the resources they use. The cloud deployment option is ideal for
organizations that want to reduce their IT infrastructure costs and need the
flexibility to scale up or down as required.
SAP NetWeaver deployment
However, the old SAP NetWeaver deployment option (i.e., SAP Business
Suite’s SAP EWM 9.5 and lower) will not be supported after 2027. This option

30
installs the WMS on a separate system that can work independently from the
central ERP system.
Non-SAP ERP system with decentralized EWM
Some clients may want to utilize a non-SAP ERP system in combination with
decentralized EWM. To simplify this procedure, SAP minimize the required
integration efforts by reintroducing IDoc integration.
Each deployment option has its own advantages and limitations. Ultimately, the
choice of deployment option depends on a variety of factors, including your
organization’s IT landscape, budget, resources, and business requirements. Let’s
delve more deeply into each deployment option next.
1.3.1 On-Premise
On-premise deployment involves the installation and execution of the SAP EWM
software suite within your own data center. This option allows complete
autonomy over the SAP EWM environment and facilitates the customization and
extension of the software to cater to specific business requirements. With the
on-premise deployment approach, warehouse users can effectively optimize
their warehouse capacities for various specializations, thereby enhancing overall
efficiency and productivity.
There are two alternatives available for on-premise deployments: embedded
EWM and decentralized EWM. Embedded EWM option integrates the SAP EWM
functionality with the SAP S/4HANA system, offering a seamless experience for
warehouse management operations within the SAP environment. Whereas the
decentralized EWM option provides a separate SAP EWM system for each
warehouse site, which can be interconnected with the SAP S/4HANA system for
centralized control and management.
Both deployment options offer their unique set of advantages, and the choice
depends on the specific business requirements and preferences. Embedded
EWM provides enhanced integration capabilities and real-time insights within
the SAP S/4HANA environment, while the decentralized EWM approach allows
for independent control and customization of each warehouse site, facilitating
greater flexibility and adaptability to varying business needs.
Let’s delve deep into these options:
© 

31
Embedded EWM
As shown in Figure 1.3, embedded EWM involves installing the WMS on the
same client as the central ERP system, enabling seamless integration between
them. As per SAP guidelines, this deployment option is best suited for small
to medium-sized warehouses since SAP EWM is embedded in a single system
for both ERP and SAP EWM.
Figure 1.3 SAP S/4HANA: Embedded EWM Deployment Option
Two versions of embedded EWM are available: basic and advanced. SAP
includes the basic SAP EWM application component in the standard SAP
S/4HANA license. However, if you want to utilize the advanced features of SAP
EWM, additional licensing is necessary.
The benefits of embedded EWM include the following:
Simplified system structure compared to decentralized EWM.
SAP S/4HANA and SAP EWM can run on the same landscape.
Embedded EWM reduces data replication by allowing business partner
data, material master data, and batch master data to be directly accessed
from SAP S/4HANA.
The Core Interface (CIF) is no longer required.
Transactional data, such as purchase order data and production order
data, can be read directly.
Elimination of the need for additional documents, such as outbound
deliveries.

32
Embedded EWM reduces costs, as the basic SAP EWM functionality is
included in the SAP S/4HANA ERP license.
The limitations of embedded EWM include the following:
The warehouse system cannot operate if the ERP system is down.
In high-volume warehouse transactions or multiple warehouses with large
material flow systems, the solution is not very flexible.
Integration with storage locations in other SAP ERP systems is not possible
with this option.

Decentralized EWM
As shown in Figure 1.4, decentralized EWM provides a dedicated system that
manages warehouse operations autonomously, separate from the central ERP
system. This approach ensures that warehouse operations can persist even
during ERP system downtime or maintenance. Furthermore, it exhibits high
scalability and can handle high-volume and high-intensity environments
proficiently. This option also facilitates integration with multiple ERP systems,
enabling logistics service providers to utilize a single warehouse to cater to
the demands of numerous business entities. In addition, this approach allows

34
the connection of decentralized EWM with SAP S/4HANA Cloud, private edition
, providing more flexibility and functionality.
Figure 1.4 SAP S/4HANA: Decentralized EWM Deployment Option
The benefits of utilizing decentralized EWM include the following:
Even if the ERP system experiences downtime, the SAP EWM system and
warehouse will remain functional, thus guaranteeing uninterrupted
warehouse operations.
Decentralized EWM is equipped to handle substantial transaction volumes,
enabling the warehouse to efficiently manage extensive inventory and
throughput.
The system can manage several warehouses within the same landscape,
furnishing more significant flexibility and authority over inventory
management.
The integrated system for SAP S/4HANA decentralized EWM and SAP
S/4HANA can be updated independently without any mutual impact,
resulting in more efficient and streamlined upgrades.
Decentralized EWM has better abilities to support automatic warehouses,
including seamless integration with material flow systems and automated
storage and retrieval systems.
The system can connect with multiple ERP systems, providing better
integration and coordination throughout the entire supply chain.
Limitations of decentralized EWM include the following:
In terms of complexity in system management, operating a decentralized
system can be more complex and challenging compared to the embedded
© 

35
EWM setup and can add increased IT infrastructure cost.
In terms of data integration issue, data replication from SAP S/4HANA to a
decentralized EWM system can sometimes add problems, and detailed
analysis will be needed to sort out issues.
Training and skill requirements, operating a decentralized system might
demand additional training and expertise for personnel managing each
individual system, potentially leading to higher training costs.
In summary, an on-premise deployment of SAP EWM provides complete
autonomy and customization opportunities to cater to specific business needs.
The embedded EWM and decentralized EWM options are available, each with
unique advantages, depending on the business requirements and preferences.
Ultimately, the choice of deployment approach can significantly impact the
efficiency and productivity of your warehouse management operations.
1.3.2 Cloud Deployment
SAP S/4HANA Cloud warehouse management is a cutting-edge software solution
that leverages the power of cloud hyperscale technology, where SAP manages
the underlying IT infrastructure. The pricing model for this solution follows a
subscription-based model common in cloud-based services. As a result, users
can benefit from continuous feature deliveries, quick time-to-value, and lower
TCO.
By deploying SAP S/4HANA Cloud Warehouse Management, organizations can
achieve operational excellence in their warehouse management processes,
streamline their supply chain operations, and improve overall efficiency. With
SAP managing the IT infrastructure, organizations can focus on their core
business processes, while leaving IT complexities to the experts.
Similar to the on-premise version, an SAP S/4HANA Cloud deployment is
available in two versions: SAP S/4HANA Cloud, private edition, and SAP S/4HANA
Cloud, public edition. SAP S/4HANA Cloud, private edition, is designed for users
who require a high degree of customization and control over their system, while
SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition, is ideal for organizations seeking a more
standardized, out-of-the-box solution. We’ll discuss each of these options next:
SAP S/4HANA Cloud, private edition
As shown in Figure 1.5, SAP S/4HANA Cloud, private edition, provides the
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

36
option for decentralized EWM or embedded EWM, enabling you to access the
same functionalities as in on-premise scenarios. This service is hosted on a
private server managed by SAP, thus ensuring efficient technical
maintenance. You have the flexibility to choose whether or not to upgrade to
newer versions.
In practical terms, the decentralized EWM deployment option allows for the
implementation of SAP EWM on a separate server, still integrated with SAP
S/4HANA. On the other hand, the embedded deployment option involves the
installation of SAP EWM directly within SAP S/4HANA. In both cases, the
service is hosted on a private server that is maintained by SAP, which means
that you can rest assured that your system will be well maintained and
updated regularly.
Figure 1.5 SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Private Edition, Deployment Option
SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition
SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition, as shown in Figure 1.6, comes with built-
in cloud-based warehouse management solution that is a version of SAP
EWM. Thus, this edition provides a comprehensive suite of warehousing
capabilities tailored to the needs of cloud-based businesses.

Figure 1.6 SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Public Edition, Deployment Options
Warehouse management in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition, is a fully
integrated solution that supports both inbound and outbound processes, as
well as internal warehouse operations such as inventory management,
physical inventory, and cycle counting. Additionally, it includes advanced
features like wave management, pick and pack optimization, and task
interleaving to streamline warehouse processes and improve efficiency.
By leveraging cloud technology, SAP S/4HANA Cloud’s warehouse
management capability allows for increased scalability, flexibility, and
reduced maintenance costs, since it eliminates the need for on-premise
hardware and software installations. It also enables real-time monitoring and
analytics, providing warehouse managers with a better understanding of their
operations and performance, and offers numerous benefits in terms of
efficiency, scalability, and cost savings.
1.3.3 SAP NetWeaver Deployments
As shown in Figure 1.7, SAP provides an additional deployment option besides
on-premise and cloud-based, which is the older SAP NetWeaver deployment
(i.e., SAP Business Suite’s SAP EWM 9.5 and earlier versions). However, according
to SAP, this option will not be supported after 2027. With this deployment
option, the WMS is installed on a separate system, enabling it to operate
independently from the central ERP system. Consequently, warehouse
operations can continue uninterrupted even when the ERP system is unavailable
or undergoing maintenance.
When utilizing the SAP Business Suite-based decentralized EWM, an SAP EWM
system can link to SAP systems from SAP R/3 4.6C onwards (including SAP R/3

1.3.4 Non-SAP ERP Systems with Decentralized EWM
As shown Figure 1.8, some customers may decide to use their own (non-SAP)

this reduction, SAP reintroduced IDoc integration, which was previously

1.4 Data Transfers between SAP ERP or SAP
S/4HANA and SAP EWM
The master data in SAP EWM is classified into two primary categories. The first
category is external data, which must be replicated from the SAP ERP or SAP
S/4HANA system into the SAP EWM environment. This external data includes
information like material master, vendor master, customer master, plant, and
other similar data. The replication of this data is a necessary step in order to
ensure accurate and up-to-date data in the SAP EWM environment.
The second category is internal data, which is created exclusively within the SAP
EWM environment. This type of data includes storage bin master data and
packaging specification master data. These data elements are typically created
when setting up the SAP EWM system and are maintained within the SAP EWM
system.
Note that the master data replication process from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to
SAP EWM is a critical component of the overall system setup. This process
ensures that the data in the SAP EWM system is consistent with the data in the
SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system. Additionally, the replication process also
ensures that any changes made to the data in the ERP or in the SAP S/4HANA
system are reflected in the SAP EWM system.
Let’s now consider the different data transfer processes, for SAP NetWeaver
deployments, embedded EWM deployments, and decentralized EWM
deployments:
Data transfer for SAP NetWeaver deployment (SAP EWM 9.5 and below)
As shown in Figure 1.9 to enable the deployment of SAP EWM 9.5 and lower
through the SAP NetWeaver SAP Business Suite, the system utilizes the CIF
technology to transfer master data between SAP ERP and SAP EWM. CIF is
primarily utilized for exchanging data between SAP ERP and SAP Supply
Chain Management (SAP SCM). However, in the case of SAP EWM, only master
data is transferred from SAP ERP to SAP EWM, and no communication occurs
in the opposite direction via CIF.
In contrast, transactional data, such as inbound and outbound delivery
documents originating from SAP ERP, are integrated into SAP EWM through
the queued remote functional call (qRFC) technology. This method allows for
© 

41
asynchronous communication between the two systems and provides a
reliable and efficient way of transferring transactional data from SAP ERP to
SAP EWM.
Figure 1.9 Data Transfer in SAP NetWeaver Deployment
Data transfer for embedded EWM
As shown in Figure 1.10, in an embedded EWM system, it is not necessary to
transfer master data through the CIF. However, note that the transmission of
transaction data from SAP S/4HANA to embedded EWM still requires the use
of qRFC technology.
qRFC is a communication method used by SAP systems to transfer data
between systems in a reliable and efficient manner. It enables data to be sent
in batches, reducing the risk of data loss or errors. In the case of embedded
EWM, transaction data includes information about goods movements,
inventory updates, and warehouse operations.
By utilizing qRFC, SAP S/4HANA can transmit transaction data to embedded
EWM in a timely and accurate manner. This capability allows for the seamless
integration between the two systems, thus enabling real-time visibility into
warehouse operations and inventory levels.
Note that, while master data transfer via CIF is not required in embedded
EWM, CIF-based data transfers may still be necessary for other SAP
components or systems. Therefore, an important step is to evaluate the
specific requirements of each scenario and determine the appropriate data
transfer method.

Data transfer for decentralized EWM
As shown in Figure 1.11, in a decentralized EWM implementation with SAP

the transfer of material master data from SAP ERP to SAP EWM. Additionally,
the data replication framework (DRF) technique is utilized for the transfer of
customer and vendor master data, commonly referred to as business partners
in decentralized EWM. In contrast, the CIF technique is still utilized for the
transfer of certain master data, such as packaging specifications, from SAP
ERP to SAP EWM.

Moreover, certain types of transactional data, such as inbound and outbound
delivery documents from SAP ERP, are integrated into SAP EWM through the
utilization of qRFC technology. This technology allows for asynchronous

are accurately and efficiently transferred from SAP ERP to SAP EWM.

a robust and reliable means of integrating SAP ERP and SAP EWM in a
decentralized EWM implementation on the SAP S/4HANA system.
